solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like writers, they branch out

parts.note: 'like' means as, in the sense 'as a ...'
pens are writing instruments, so writers

explanation.surface: A wry remark that authors, like trees, keep sending out new shoots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch out' reads as authors diversifying, but it is literal: trees have branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar trees of this kind have branches, so as a plural they are things that branch out.

clue.text: Direction followed by parasites to cut through

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Instructions for some grim procedure: point the way, then let the bloodsuckers bore in.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve a thin piece off something is to cut through it with a blade.

clue.text: Lace first treated to produce a brilliant effect

indicators.note: producing something new from the letters signals that they are reworked into a fresh order
first means only the opening letter of the word treated is used

explanation.surface: A craft instruction: dress the lace before anything else and it will dazzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes T from 'treated'; that T joins LACE and 'to produce' signals the rearrangement of those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word means striking brilliance of performance or display, a dazzling effect.

clue.text: Submissive like a mid-European

definitions.meaning: resembling a Slav, a person from central or eastern Europe

explanation.surface: An unkind stereotype that people from central Europe are meek and compliant.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as Slav-ish, a jokey coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Servile and obedient behaviour is the ordinary meaning; the joke reading means resembling a Slav.

clue.text: The starting point in court proceedings

definitions.text: The starting point in court proceedings

parts.words: The starting point in court proceedings
parts.note: sounds like the opening of a lawsuit, but the court is a tennis court, where the server stands at the back line to begin each point

explanation.surface: Where a trial in a court of law begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court, not a law court: play starts with the server behind the line at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a reference point for comparison, and in tennis the back line from which serves are struck.

clue.text: Light brown unglazed pot

definitions.meaning: pottery fired once and left without glaze, also called bisque

explanation.surface: A catalogue description of a pale tan earthenware vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pale tan shade and also once-fired pottery that has not yet been glazed.

clue.text: After first shouting you are sounding serious — that's bizarre!

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word shouting
sounding means the words 'you are' are written as they are said, in text-speak letters

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like UR
real as in 'this is serious, it's for real'

explanation.surface: Someone yells and then insists they mean it, and the onlooker finds the whole scene odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just places the S at the front; 'you are' said aloud is the two letters U and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamlike and weird, like the art movement of Dali, so bizarre is a close synonym.

clue.text: A successful doubles partnership

parts.note: sounds like a winning tennis pair, but the doubles are a couple and the partnership a marriage built on affection

explanation.surface: A tennis pairing that wins in the doubles.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis love is zero, so the phrase also hints at a game where one side scores nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made for affection rather than money or status is a happy partnership of two.

clue.text: The invisible man?

parts.note: suggests the H. G. Wells story, but means someone officially ignored or erased, as if they did not exist

explanation.surface: A reference to the novel about a scientist who cannot be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone treated as having no existence, airbrushed out by a regime, is socially unseen.

clue.text: Former champion makes a couple of points about a claim to be sick

indicators.note: about means the two points sit around the other piece

parts.note: two compass points, west and south
a claim of being ill: 'ill I am'

explanation.surface: A former title holder pleads illness, perhaps to get out of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill I am' is the claim; W and S go round it. Venus and Serena of that surname are former tennis champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both tennis sisters of that surname won many Grand Slam titles, so either is a former champion.

clue.text: A number in the band showing real enthusiasm

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the band

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: One song played by a group is greeted with wild excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical but is a ring, as on a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Raving fans are wildly enthusiastic, as in a raving success or raving about something.

clue.text: A spinner has a cute fringe arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters is a new order of them

explanation.surface: A spinning top or dancer sports a sweetly styled fringe of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that spins samples at speed to separate them is a spinner.

clue.text: Swarm back to join up

indicators.note: back means the word for swarm is read backwards

parts.note: to teem is to swarm, be crowded with

explanation.surface: Bees swarm back to the hive to regroup.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together or converge at one place is a synonym of join up.

clue.text: Releases popular short hit

parts.note: drops, as in drops a single or lets go
hot as in currently in demand

explanation.surface: A music headline: the record label puts out a brief chart success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short hit' sounds like a brief chart song, but it is a tennis shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis stroke that barely clears the net and lands short is a softly played hit.

clue.text: About to fall on a circular tour

parts.note: round means about, as in 'round the house'
to trip is to stumble or fall

explanation.surface: Someone is on the verge of tumbling during a sightseeing loop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to fall' reads as imminent tumbling but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey out and back to the starting point is a circular tour.

clue.text: One for takng a view from below

definitions.text: One for takng a view from below

parts.words: One for takng a view from below
parts.note: sounds like a person with a humble viewpoint, but means an optical tube used from beneath the surface

explanation.surface: Someone who likes to see things from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's sighting tube with mirrors lets crew look out from below the waterline.

clue.text: The French experiment is a la mode

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the'
a test is a trial or experiment

explanation.surface: A fashion note: the French trial run is all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode means fashionable, and the newest style is the most up to date.

clue.text: In one month, we hear, you are twice a champion

indicators.note: in means the other letters go inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of the year

indicators.note: we hear means the words are written as they sound: you as U, and are, said twice, as R R

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like URR

explanation.surface: Someone is told that within a month they will be a double winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy of that surname won Wimbledon twice, in 2013 and 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish tennis player won Wimbledon and Olympic titles, so he is a champion.

clue.text: Produced and given away

definitions.meaning: as a field produces a crop
surrendered or conceded, as in giving ground

explanation.surface: Something was made and then handed over to others.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both bearing crops or returns and conceding or surrendering something.

clue.text: Drive on the left or right

definitions.text: Drive on the left or right

parts.words: Drive on the left or right
parts.note: sounds like road rules, but a drive is a tennis stroke, struck on whichever side matches the player's playing hand

explanation.surface: A question of which side of the road motorists use.
explanation.walkthrough: The stroke is on the right for a right-hander and on the left for a left-hander.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis drive played with the palm facing the ball, on the side of the racket hand, is this stroke.

clue.text: A leading racketeer who dined with the Queen a couple of times

parts.note: fed means ate, dined

indicators.note: a couple of times means the royal letters appear twice

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A mafia boss who has been a guest at a royal banquet twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racketeer' suggests a gangster but means a player with a racket: Roger of that surname, the Swiss tennis great.
explanation.definitionFit: A top tennis player wields a racket, so he is jokingly a leading racketeer.

clue.text: Unusual tool to create a Celtic delicacy

parts.note: rare means unusual, uncommon
a bit is a drilling tool

explanation.surface: An odd implement is used to make a traditional Welsh dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, a dish from Wales, a Celtic nation.

clue.text: Rome's mid-month show about to cause a minor diversion

indicators.text: about to cause a minor diversion
indicators.note: the opening letter takes a short detour round to the far end of the word

parts.note: side means pretentious show, as in 'putting on side'

explanation.surface: A Roman spectacle in mid-month is about to cause a small distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SIDE moves from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar this was the 15th or 13th day of the month, its midpoint.

clue.text: What finally emerges to stop a small professional channel

parts.note: to end is to stop
pro is short for professional
a duct is a small channel or pipe

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to block a minor professional TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The final result of a process is what comes out at the finish.

clue.text: The point at which an advantage always follows.

definitions.text: The point at which an advantage always follows.

parts.words: The point at which an advantage always follows.
parts.note: sounds like a general maxim, but in tennis the score of forty-all is always followed by advantage to one side

explanation.surface: A general remark that a benefit inevitably comes after a certain moment.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, from forty-all the next point won gives a player 'advantage'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tennis score at forty-all, from which the next point won gives a player advantage.

clue.text: With business static a dreaded group of activists appear within

indicators.note: the letters appear within the run of words static a dreaded

explanation.surface: Business has stalled, and a feared band of militants is turning up inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small core of trained party activists or revolutionaries is such a group.

clue.text: Alternative place to cross a river in Suffolk

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a ford is a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: A tip about another shallow crossing point on an East Anglian river.
explanation.walkthrough: Orford is a coastal village in Suffolk, an English county, known for its castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is that of a village with a castle on the coast of that East Anglian county.

clue.text: Comes back about outer limits

parts.note: re means about, concerning
bounds are boundaries, outer limits

explanation.surface: Someone returns after roaming to the very edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball that springs back off a surface returns, so the verb means comes back.

clue.text: The yachtsman's bar that reps read about

indicators.note: about means the letters of the words are moved around

explanation.surface: Sales representatives pore over a piece of sailing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a drinking spot; it is a spar on a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: On a yacht, a horizontal strut that holds the shrouds out from the mast is a bar of this name.

clue.text: Designed to look like the ocean

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Something made to resemble the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorated or styled around a central motif, like a party, means designed to a concept.
